title: Shared Opening of Every Word
statement:
You get a list of lowercase strings words. Return the longest string that every word in the list starts with.

If the words share no first letter (or one of them is empty), return the empty string "".

examples.why: All three start with "rea". The fourth letters are 'c', 'c' and 'd', so the shared part stops there.
The first two share "carp", but the third word cuts it down. Comparing only a pair of words is not enough.
An empty word shares nothing with anything.

constraints: words[i] has only lowercase English letters
hints: The answer can never be longer than the shortest word. Which word is a safe place to start reading from?
Look at the words column by column: position 0 in every word, then position 1, and so on.
Walk the columns of the first word. Stop at the first column where some word is too short or has a different letter; everything before that column is the answer.

explain.intuition:
Line the words up under each other and read down the columns. The shared opening is every column, from the left, where all the words have the same letter. The first column that breaks the pattern, because a letter differs or a word has ended, is where the answer stops.

Any single word can serve as the ruler for the columns, because the answer is a prefix of every word. Using the first word is the simplest choice. A neat alternative is to sort the list: the first and last strings in sorted order are the most different, so their shared opening is the shared opening of everything in between.
steps: For each column i of first, check every word.
If some word has length i or a different letter at i, return first.slice(0, i).
If every column of first matched, the whole first word is the answer.
pitfalls: Comparing only two words. In ["carpet", "carport", "cat"] the first pair shares more than the whole list does.
Reading past the end of a shorter word. The length check must come before the letter check.
Forgetting the single-word case: then the whole word is the answer.

solutions.title: Column-by-column scan
solutions.idea: Use the first word as the ruler and check one column at a time across all words.

solutions.title: Sort, then compare the two ends
solutions.idea: After sorting, the first and last words differ the most. Their shared opening is shared by every word between them.

followups: The list is fixed but you get many queries asking for the shared opening of a word and the list. Would a trie help?
Can you binary search on the length of the answer? What does each check cost?
